retrieved_evidence.text: When multiple policies apply to a given query, they are combined using OR for permissive policies, which are the default, or using AND for restrictive policies.
Restrictive policies are combined with AND, so a row must pass every restrictive policy in addition to at least one permissive policy to be visible.

When row security is enabled on a table (with ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY), all normal access to the table for selecting rows or modifying rows must be allowed by a row security policy. If no policy exists for the table, a default-deny policy is used, so that no rows are visible or updatable.
Superusers and roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute always bypass the row security system when accessing a table.
The table's owner is typically not subject to row security policies, though a table owner can choose to be subject to row security with ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.

retrieved_evidence.text: The table's owner is typically not subject to row security policies, though a table owner can choose to be subject to row security with ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.

When row security is enabled on a table (with ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY), all normal access to the table for selecting rows or modifying rows must be allowed by a row security policy. If no policy exists for the table, a default-deny policy is used, so that no rows are visible or updatable.
Superusers and roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute always bypass the row security system when accessing a table.
When multiple policies apply to a given query, they are combined using OR for permissive policies, which are the default, or using AND for restrictive policies.
The OR behavior of permissive policies is similar to the rule that a given role has the privileges of all roles that it is a member of.

CREATE POLICY defines a new row-level security policy for a table. The policy name must be unique per table, and the policy applies to the roles named in its TO clause, or to PUBLIC if no roles are named.
Policies can be specified for SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or ALL commands. A policy for ALL applies to every command type.

When row security is enabled on a table (with ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY), all normal access to the table for selecting rows or modifying rows must be allowed by a row security policy.
